inputs.text: National test of the UK Emergency Alerts system. Approved English text: "This is a test of Emergency Alerts, a new UK government service that will warn you if there’s a life-threatening emergency nearby. In a real emergency, follow the instructions in the alert to keep yourself and others safe. Visit gov.uk/alerts for more information. This is a test. You do not need to take any action." A Welsh version of the same text is required for the bilingual alert in Wales.

requested_area.areaDesc: Wales (bilingual version); the English-only version went to the rest of the UK

fields.description: This is a test of Emergency Alerts, a new UK government service that will warn you if there's a life-threatening emergency nearby. Visit gov.uk/alerts for more information. This is a test. You do not need to take any action.
fields.event: National test of UK Emergency Alerts
fields.headline: TEST: UK Emergency Alerts national test - no action needed
fields.instruction: In a real emergency, follow the instructions in the alert to keep yourself and others safe. This is a test. You do not need to take any action.
left_out: Welsh-language text: the input says a Welsh version is required for Wales, but no approved Welsh text was supplied. I did not write my own translation, because unapproved wording should not go out on an official alert. An approved Welsh text must be added before the bilingual alert is sent to Wales.

Part of the approved English text: the full approved text is over the 280-character limit for the description. The sentence 'In a real emergency, follow the instructions in the alert to keep yourself and others safe.' was moved to the instruction field instead.
fields.note_for_reviewer: 1) The approved text was split across description and instruction to fit the length limit; confirm this is acceptable or whether the approved wording must be sent in full. 2) Status is set to Exercise as the context directs, though CAP 'Test' could also apply to a system test (CAP 'Test' means recipients should ignore the message, which may not suit a public test). Note that the Welsh text is still missing for the Wales bilingual alert.
